classification_rationale: The 'service stop path' clause is false: the Windows SCM stop handler (service_win.cpp:109-161,259) and the POSIX watcher (main.cpp:825) both call Agent::stop(), which sets stop_requested_ and does not shut plugins down; run() then takes its NORMAL final teardown, which drains the pool FIRST (agent.cpp:3566) and shuts plugins down afterwards (~3646-3655) - the opposite order. Only an early return out of run() (registration rejection, PKI persist/rebuild bail-outs) or an escaping exception (service_win.cpp wraps run() in a try/catch; main.cpp:939 is bare, so on Linux an escaping exception is std::terminate) reaches the Run()-exit ScopeExit ordering (agent.cpp:1142-1159), plus a stop observed in the reconnect loop's backoff/top with no live stream. Code behaviour (shutdown() does not reset) is correct on every ordering, so the facts derive IMPACT I9 -> INFO -> NICE; reporters' native labels LOW/INFO/SHOULD(cpp-safety). A false rationale next to the control-flow decision is a truth finding (the skill's exception), but it could mislead a future maintainer into re-adding the reset - hence recorded, not dismissed. This is the residue of f1: the delta's rewording introduced the new false half. The README sentence ('when run() unwinds and the agent shuts plugins down') and the JSON are accurate; the new test's header comment ('when run() unwinds') is accurate. Row recorded by the orchestrator from the reporter's report.
